result.title: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development
result.summary: Games are a rich testbed for visual agents, demanding perception, long-horizon planning, and precise control. However, collecting human gameplay is costly, and learning from gameplay videos requires inferring missing actions. Existing datasets also cover a limited range of games, often without explicit tasks or verifiable outcomes. To address these gaps, we introduce Game2Player, a framework that co-develops game environments and players to collect diverse and verifiable gameplay experience at scale. In the Game2Player loop, a Builder agent adapts existing web games, exposes their internal state, and defines tasks with state-based progress measures and success checks. A Coding Player and a VLM Player then attempt the tasks and report problems to the Builder for repair, so that play serves as both environment validation and training data collection. With Game2Player, we build 568 verified web games with 3,436 tasks, collect 15.7K trajectories (307 hours of gameplay), and hold out 50 games as the benchmark PlayerBench. To evaluate the collected experience as training data, we train VLM agents with progress-weighted SFT, assigning greater weight to steps that advance task progress. Game2Player-9B improves progress from 14.3% to 31.2% on PlayerBench and from 30.0% to 53.1% on the external GameWorld benchmark. More broadly, our work suggests a path for visual agents to scale their gameplay experience by building, verifying, and learning from existing game worlds.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 Game2Player 框架，让 Builder agent 改造网页游戏并暴露内部状态、定义带状态进度度量的任务，再由 Coding Player 与 VLM Player 试玩并回报问题，从而同时完成环境验证与大规模可验证 gameplay 轨迹采集，并用 progress-weighted SFT 训练 VLM agent。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文主线是游戏环境与数据规模化，而非 latent 推理；但「progress-weighted SFT」按是否推进任务进度加权各步监督，可供核查其在轨迹训练与贡献分配上的借鉴价值，能否迁移到 latent 推理步骤加权尚不确定。
